sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: one small rainy island in the north atlantic ruled around a quarter of

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: all the land on earth and roughly one in every five human beings alive

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: it ruled india and canada australia and egypt nigeria kenya jamaica

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: malaysia hong kong and dozens of tiny islands most people couldnt find on a map

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: It was so spread out across the globe that people said the sun never set on it.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: At any hour of the day, it was daytime somewhere in the British Empire.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: And the strangest part: for most of its history, it wasn’t really run by the British government at all.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: it was built by pirates the queen secretly shared profits with by a company

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: that had its own private army twice the size of the british army by merchants

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: adventurers and investors chasing money

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: It gave the world railways, cricket, and the language you’re hearing right now.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: it also shipped millions of africans across the ocean and chains watched famines kill millions

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: and drew borders that people are still fighting over today

sentence_labels.label: question
sentence_labels.text: So how did a country with fewer people than many modern cities end up ruling a quarter of the planet?

sentence_labels.label: question
sentence_labels.text: And how did it lose almost all of it in just a few decades?

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: to understand that we have to go back to a time when england

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: was poor small and completely left out of the race to grab the world

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: In the 1500s, the superpowers of the world weren’t English.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: They were Spanish and Portuguese.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: After Columbus reached the Americas in 1492, Spain and Portugal didn’t waste any time.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: in 1494 with the pope blessing

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: they signed a treaty that basically split the whole newly discovered world between the two of them

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: A line on the map: everything on one side for Spain, everything on the other side for Portugal.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: England wasn’t even part of the conversation.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: Soon, Spanish ships were sailing home from Mexico and Peru loaded with mountains of silver and gold.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: Spain became the richest country in Europe.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: England, meanwhile, was a small, fairly poor country on the edge of the map with only a few million people.

sentence_labels.label: conclusion
sentence_labels.text: So England’s Queen Elizabeth I came up with a solution.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: If you can’t find your own treasure, take someone else’s.

sentence_labels.label: explain
sentence_labels.text: she didnt have the money to build a big navy

sentence_labels.label: twist
sentence_labels.text: but england had plenty of tough ambitious sea captains so she gave some of them a special license
